trust_decision.summary: A JMS message's type-id property is turned into a Java type for deserialization in MappingJackson2MessageConverter.getJavaTypeForMessage: the untrusted string is resolved with ClassUtils.forName and handed to ObjectMapper.readValue, with no trusted-package gate. The decision is whether that type id's package is allowed, taken before class resolution.

landing_point.why: The fix commit names this converter, and getJavaTypeForMessage is the only place in it where a type id taken from a message property becomes a JavaType; the supported sibling JacksonJsonMessageConverter already carries the identical guard, so this method is the single unprotected spot.

fix_sites.entry_point: MappingJackson2MessageConverter.fromMessage(jakarta.jms.Message), reached from MessageListenerContainer / JmsTemplate receive paths
fix_sites.module_kind: spring-jms module, deprecated Jackson 2 message converter

O3_reason_to_dismiss: Even at the fix site itself a solver can argue dismissal: the class is @Deprecated(since 7.0, forRemoval) in favour of JacksonJsonMessageConverter, which already has trustedPackages, so the legacy converter can look like it needs no new security feature.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: The unconfigured default must stay permissive and configured type-id aliases must keep resolving unchecked: existing tests deserialize java.lang.Object, java.util.HashMap and MyBean with no trusted packages set, and setTypeIdMappings short ids return before the guard. A deny-by-default or alias-gated fix breaks them.

O6_input_shapes: empty trusted list (setTrustedPackages() denies every type id)
configured type-id alias via setTypeIdMappings (guard not applied)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a Jackson message converter in another package that resolves the payload type from transport headers instead of a method parameter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: STOMP frames carry arbitrary user headers and the messaging converters already sit on a MessageHeaders abstraction, so a maintainer adding a __TypeId__-style header resolution for destination-agnostic reply handling is a natural extension.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: a delegating JMS converter that resolves the type id from the JMS property itself before handing the body to a payload converter
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: MessagingMessageConverter already extracts and maps JMS headers, so resolving a type id there before delegation is a small, plausible refactor of the same job.

O9_family: CWE-502 deserialization of untrusted data: attacker-controlled type id resolved to an arbitrary class and instantiated via Jackson

O10_build.toolchain: Gradle 9.5.1 via wrapper (gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties:3); Java 17+ (framework-docs/modules/ROOT/pages/overview.adoc:9); Jackson 2 and Jackson 3 are optional deps of spring-jms (spring-jms/spring-jms.gradle:13,17)
O10_build.project_tests: Mockito unit tests in spring-jms/src/test/java/org/springframework/jms/support/converter: MappingJackson2MessageConverterTests and JacksonJsonMessageConverterTests, no broker needed; other spring-jms tests use embedded Artemis (spring-jms/spring-jms.gradle:24-25).

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add setTrustedPackages plus a plain package-equality guard in getJavaTypeForMessage, missing the [L/[[L array descriptors and the default-permissive and type-id-alias behaviour.

out_of_scope_notes: spring-oxm's XStreamMarshaller resolves class names from payload data (spring-oxm/src/main/java/org/springframework/oxm/xstream/XStreamMarshaller.java:515,603) under its own supportedClasses/permission model; that is a different protection from this advisory and was not pursued.

spring-messaging's Jackson converters take the target class from the caller (spring-messaging/src/main/java/org/springframework/messaging/converter/AbstractMessageConverter.java:170-180), not from message headers, so they are not routes into this sink.
unverified: repo_mb: no shell was available to measure the tree; the repo is far above 5 MB and far below 1.5 GB, so neither tiny_repo nor giant_repo applies.
The advisory text itself was not supplied, only its summary line; that both converter classes are named in it is inferred from the summary ('Jackson JMS Converters') and the fix commit subject.

That the parent commit fe68e337b2 introduced the sibling's trustedPackages support is inferred from the pinned tree (JacksonJsonMessageConverter.java:121-125 '@since 7.0.8' plus its tests) and the commit list, not from reading that commit's diff.
